# Team Pong

> A party Pong game: the TV shows the field, every player's phone is a bat, teams of up to four play left against right.

The pages declare WebMCP tools (document.modelContext.registerTool), so an AI agent in the visitor's browser can use them
instead of the buttons. Today that works in Chrome with WebMCP switched on (chrome://flags/#enable-webmcp-testing).

## Pages

- /screen: the TV screen with the field, the room code and the score.
- /: the phone page, a join form and then the bat pad; the game master's phone also has the match controls.
- /host: the game-master controls for a laptop, without a bat.

## Tools on /screen

- describe: what the TV screen shows and which tools it has.
- get_state: the room code, teams with player names, score, phase, seconds left and every bat's position.

## Tools on / (the phone page)

- describe: which part of the page shows now (join form, bat pad or lost connection) and the tools it offers.
- join {room, name, team}: join the room on the TV, as the Join button does.
- move_bat {x, y, angle}: move this player's bat, as a finger on the pad does; out-of-range values are clamped.

## Game-master tools (the game master's phone and /host, only while it is game master)

- set_rules {mode, value}: choose a timed match ("time", minutes) or first to a number of goals ("score").
- start: start the match, as the Start button does.
- pause: pause the match, or resume it when paused.
- end: end the match now and show the winner.

## Tools on /host

- describe: what the page shows now, whether it is game master, and the tools it offers.
